content: The medication combination of desogestrel and ethinyl estradiol is sometimes used off-label for conditions such as dysmenorrhea, dysfunctional uterine bleeding, endometriosis, polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS), and acne. It is not recommended for use in premenarchal individuals. Desogestrel can reduce the effectiveness of cabotegravir by increasing its metabolism, which is contraindicated. Ethinyl estradiol can increase the levels or effects of fezolinetant by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism, which is contraindicated. Co-administration with CYP1A2 inhibitors can increase fezolinetant's plasma concentration. Amobarbital decreases the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives, so nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the effects of anastrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Anastrozole should not be used concurrently with estrogen-containing products. Apalutamide decreases the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Armodafinil reduces the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended during co-administration. Atazanavir can alter the levels of ethinyl estradiol, leading to significant changes in estrogen plasma levels. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Belzutifan decreases the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, which may lead to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are advised, as belzutifan may also cause fetal harm based on animal studies. Bosentan reduces the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Brigatinib decreases the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Women should use effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for at least four months after the last dose, as brigatinib may cause fetal harm.
